program_overview.title: A Level Further Maths: Core Pure and Applied Options
program_overview.tagline: The second maths A level, taught as a subject of its own: complex numbers, matrices, proof and differential equations, then the applied options your board sets.
program_overview.description:
Further Maths is a full A level that sits on top of A level Maths. The boards are clear about the relationship: OCR states that learners are assumed to know the content of GCSE Mathematics and A Level Mathematics, and Pearson Edexcel says the students who benefit most are likely to hold A level Maths. In practice most students take the two side by side across Years 12 and 13, and this course is timed to run alongside our A Level Maths course or your school's.

Every board splits Further Maths into a compulsory pure core and a set of options. Edexcel 9FM0 has two Core Pure papers plus two options chosen from Further Pure, Further Statistics, Further Mechanics and Decision Maths. AQA 7367 has two papers on compulsory content and a third paper on two of mechanics, statistics and discrete mathematics. OCR A H245 has Pure Core papers Y540 and Y541 plus two optional papers, and OCR MEI H645 has the Core Pure paper Y420 with a major option or a set of minor options. We teach the shared core to everyone and the options your school or exam centre has entered you for.

The first nine months cover the AS-standard core and the first applied option. Months 10 to 16 take the core to full A level depth, from de Moivre's theorem to second-order differential equations, and finish the options. The final two months are revision and past papers under real timing, matched to your board's paper structure and marked against official schemes. Classes are live and small, so the teacher reads your working as you write it.
what_makes_this_different: Built from the boards' own specifications: Edexcel 9FM0, AQA 7367, OCR A H245 and OCR MEI H645, with your board's paper structure driving the practice phase
Sequenced to run alongside A Level Maths, so each Further Maths topic arrives after the A level Maths skill it leans on, not before
Proof treated as a skill in its own right: induction, contradiction and the writing of a complete argument are practised every month, not saved for one chapter
Options taught to your entry, whether that is mechanics, statistics, decision or discrete maths, or further pure, rather than a generic mixture
Calculator technique for matrices, complex numbers and distributions taught explicitly, alongside the work that must be done by hand
Two full months of past papers under real timing, marked against official mark schemes, with an error clinic after every paper

learning_path.phase_1: Core Pure, first year: proof by induction, complex numbers and the Argand diagram, matrices and transformations, roots of polynomials, series and vectors in three dimensions

learning_path.phase_3: Core Pure, second year: de Moivre and complex roots, further calculus, Maclaurin series, polar coordinates, hyperbolic functions and differential equations
learning_path.phase_4: Applied option two and option depth: the second option, and both options taken to full A level standard
learning_path.phase_5: Revision and the past-paper cycle: structured revision by strand, then full papers under timing with marked review

career_outcomes: The full Further Maths content for your board, with two months kept for revision and papers
Fluency with the question styles of your own board, built on official past papers and mark schemes

faqs.question: Is Further Maths harder than A level Maths?
faqs.answer: It goes further rather than simply faster. The boards assume you already know A level Maths: OCR's specification says learners are assumed to know the content of GCSE Mathematics and A Level Mathematics. Further Maths then adds topics that feel new to most students, such as complex numbers, matrices, proof by induction, polar coordinates and differential equations. Many students find the step up is in abstraction and in writing complete arguments, which is why we practise proof every month.

faqs.question: Can I take Further Maths online?
faqs.answer: You can be taught Further Maths online, and this course covers the full content live with a teacher. The exams themselves are sat in person, either at your school or college or at an exam centre that accepts private candidates. We teach the course; your school or exam centre makes the exam entry.

faqs.question: Do I need Further Maths for a maths degree?
faqs.answer: It depends on the university and the course. Some mathematics courses require Further Maths, some prefer it and some do not ask for it. Check the current entry requirements on the page of each course you are interested in. We teach the subject; we do not give admissions advice.

faqs.question: Which exam boards do you cover?
faqs.answer: AQA 7367, Edexcel 9FM0, OCR A H245 and OCR MEI H645. All four have a compulsory pure core and a choice of applied or further pure options. Edexcel has two Core Pure papers and two option papers. AQA has two papers on compulsory content and a third on two optional applications. OCR A has Pure Core papers Y540 and Y541 and two optional papers. OCR MEI has the Core Pure paper Y420 plus a major option or minor options. We teach the core to everyone and your entered options in detail.

faqs.question: Can I study Further Maths without A level Maths?
faqs.answer: Not sensibly on its own. Pearson Edexcel lists no formal prior learning requirement, but says the students who benefit most are likely to hold A level Maths, and OCR assumes its content throughout. Most students take the two together across Years 12 and 13. If you are not yet studying A level Maths, our A Level Maths course runs alongside this one.

faqs.question: Which options do you teach: mechanics, statistics or decision?
faqs.answer: All of them, matched to your board: further mechanics, further statistics, decision or discrete mathematics, and further pure options. Tell us which options your school or exam centre has chosen and those are the ones we teach in depth. If the choice has not been made yet, the first lessons include a conversation about which route suits you.

faqs.question: My school does not offer Further Maths. Can I still do it?
faqs.answer: Yes. This course teaches the whole qualification, and you can sit the exams as a private candidate at an exam centre that accepts private candidates. You arrange the entry with the centre; we make sure the teaching covers every paper on your board's specification.

faqs.question: When should I start?
faqs.answer: The beginning of Year 12, alongside A level Maths, is the natural point, because Further Maths topics are timed to follow the A level Maths skills they need. Students who join later take a diagnostic in the first week and get a catch-up plan.

faqs.question: How are the classes run?
faqs.answer: Live online classes with a real teacher, either in a group of 15 to 20 students at a similar level or one to one. Homework is marked with method-mark comments, and there is WhatsApp support between classes. Current fees for your region are shown in the pricing section of this page.

faqs.question: Can I try a lesson before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Yes. Book a free demo class first. The teacher works through some Further Maths with you, finds where you are, and suggests whether group or one-to-one teaching fits better. There is no obligation to enrol.
